ogTitle: Kenmore Tile Installation for Split-Levels by the Lake
ogDesc: Showers, floors and backsplashes across Kenmore's split-levels and lakeside homes — pre-sloped bases, bonded membranes, and a photographed 24-hour flood test before a tile is set. (425) 595-1079.

roles.heroLead: A shower's waterproofing is never the surface you scrub — it's the bonded layer underneath. In a Kenmore split-level, where lake-end humidity already works on every bathroom, that layer separates a shower with twenty quiet years ahead of it from a $40,000 framing repair. We build it, flood it for 24 hours, photograph the standing water, then start tiling.
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Kenmore, WA?
roles.costP1: Installed tile in Kenmore lands around $14–$26 per square foot when tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor all go in the total; the labor line begins at $11/sq ft. For a standard tub-shower surround, plan $3,200–$6,800. For a bathroom done completely — floor plus shower plus niche — most projects settle between $6,500 and $14,000.
roles.costP2: One quiet variable outweighs the sticker: tile format. Labor tracks cuts and grout lines, so a $4 mosaic sheet often installs for more money than a $12 large-format porcelain plank — the invoice never sees it coming.
roles.costNote: Kenmore ranges as of August 2026, installed — materials, tile and labor combined. Your free estimate produces the written number that actually holds.
roles.layersLead: Count them: seven layers from framing to grout. Every leaking shower we open around Kenmore skipped at least one — the membrane most often — trading a few hundred dollars up front for a five-figure tear-out down the road.
roles.whyP1: Failure here is silent by design. Water clears the grout, saturates the substrate, and only announces itself a couple of years on — a floor that gives slightly in the hallway, a shadow on the ceiling below. The repair by then reads framing, subfloor, drywall, full re-tile.
roles.whyP2: Of everything in a shower's budget, waterproofing is about a tenth. Removing it is the most expensive edit anyone can make to a bathroom remodel.
roles.scopeIntro: Prices shown are starting points; format, the substrate we uncover, and layout complexity each shift them. The binding number gets written at your home, free.
roles.cardShower: Assembly first: pre-sloped base, bonded membrane, a flood test with photos, then the niche and the curb (or curbless entry), and finally tile. The layer you never see again is the one doing the work.
roles.cardFloors: Bathrooms, kitchens, mudrooms, entries and daylight basements. Subfloor leveled flat, with an uncoupling layer added when movement or radiant heat is in play.
roles.cardBacksplash: Mosaic sheet, subway, herringbone or slab-look porcelain — outlets cut clean, edges trimmed, grout keyed to the countertop instead of whatever the tile box suggests.
roles.cardHeated: An electric radiant mat laid over uncoupling membrane, resistance-checked on both sides of the setting bed, on its own dedicated circuit. Sensible only while the floor is open.
roles.cardRepair: Failed grout, cracked tile, shower corners letting go. Our first job is telling you honestly whether a repair holds or the substrate below has quit.
roles.cardDemo: Old tile, backer and thinset come out under sheeting and negative air; every scrap gets hauled. No pile appears beside your garage.
roles.materialsLead: In Kenmore bathrooms the usual tile mistake is technical, not aesthetic — a perfectly good tile asked to do a job it can't. Here's the short course we'd give you at the estimate.
roles.materialsNote: These are material rates only, before install. Samples ride along to the visit, with a frank word on which earn their price.
roles.estIntro: Same variables our estimator works through at your door — scope, footage, format and prep. Planning math, not a commitment.
roles.daysLead: For a typical Kenmore bathroom, four to six working days. The two that seem slow — waterproofing and its flood test — are the two doing the real work.

roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Kenmore, WA?
roles.faqA1: Kenmore tile installation totals somewhere near $14 to $26 per square foot installed — that includes the tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor, and labor by itself begins near $11 per square foot. Tub-shower surrounds in the standard footprint price at $3,200 to $6,800, while a bathroom taken to completion — floor, shower and niche — typically runs $6,500 to $14,000. The format you pick moves cost more than the tile's own price: mosaic sheets and large-format tile each ask for much more labor per square foot than ordinary 12×12.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Kenmore?
roles.faqA2: A standard alcove shower in Kenmore prices at $3,200 to $6,800, covering demolition, a bonded waterproofing system, the pre-sloped pan or base, tile setting, a niche and grout. Push into curbless entries, benches, steam or full-height stone and the number climbs past that range. Waterproofing accounts for roughly a tenth of the cost while heading off the failure that carries a five-figure repair bill.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Every time — and in a lake-end city like Kenmore we'd argue it matters double. The system is bonded, not improvised: pre-sloped base, sheet or liquid membrane taken up every wall, corners, seams and penetrations all sealed, then a documented 24-hour flood test before tiling begins. Cement board alone is not a water barrier. Tile and grout let water through; the membrane is what stops it reaching framing.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Plan four to six working days for a Kenmore bathroom. The sequence: demolition with dust protection, then substrate and waterproofing with the 24-hour flood test behind it, then one to two days setting tile, then grout, silicone and trim. Hold off using the shower for a further 24 hours while grout cures. A floor on its own generally takes one or two days.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Porcelain wins anywhere water or traffic shows up: it's the denser body, takes on less than 0.5% water, and resists chips. Ceramic remains the economical pick for walls and backsplashes. Around Kenmore we put porcelain on every floor and shower floor without exception, and let ceramic or glass handle the vertical surfaces.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes — and against a damp Kenmore morning it's a small daily pleasure. Electric radiant mat under tile adds $11 to $16 per square foot installed with the thermostat counted in, and because it only pencils while the floor is already up, it's the least expensive luxury a bathroom can add. Installation goes over an uncoupling membrane, with resistance checks before and after setting, on a dedicated circuit.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Nearly always. Tear-out with haul-away costs about $3.50 per square foot and gives us the one honest look at your subfloor — moisture history, rot, movement — while keeping floor heights correct at every doorway. Setting new tile over old is possible when the existing floor is flat, solid and well bonded, but it lifts the floor and hides conditions we would much rather discover at demo than after grout.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Kenmore?
roles.faqA8: Kitchen backsplashes in Kenmore run $1,100 to $2,200 installed for a typical 30-square-foot span — outlet cutting, edge trim and grout matched to the counters in the price. Expect the upper half of the range for mosaic sheets, herringbone layouts, a picture-framed panel behind the range, or slab-look porcelain taken full height; the added layout and cutting time is the driver.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Quite often. Repair and regrout begins at $8 per square foot and fits when grout is stained or breaking up, an impact took out a couple tiles, or the corners of the shower need grout replaced with silicone. It stops fitting when the substrate has failed — tiles that sound hollow, loosen in a spreading pattern, or sit on a wall with give. In that case a repair buys months, not years, and we tell you which situation is yours before quoting.
roles.faqQ10: Which Kenmore neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: All of Kenmore — Moorlands, Arrowhead, Inglewood, Uplake, Lakepointe, Downtown Kenmore, Norway Hill and Waynita — plus the neighbors we cross into daily: Lake Forest Park, Sheridan Beach, Finn Hill, Juanita, Bothell, Brier, North City and Mountlake Terrace, and onward across the Northshore, the Eastside and Seattle.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: A 2-year workmanship warranty from OC Flooring stands behind every tile installation — twice our carpet term, since tile trouble tends to surface in the second year, not the second week. Where we install a manufacturer's complete assembly, their waterproofing system warranty applies as well. And because we photograph both membrane and flood test, the documentation exists whenever the house changes hands.
roles.hoodsOut: Don't spot your street? An hour's radius around Kenmore is all workable — just say so when you book.
